# Mahāpajāpatigotamītherīapadāna (Thi-Ap 17)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāpajāpatigotamītherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 17) is an account in the Therīapadāna section of the Apadāna collection belonging to the late sutta stratum of the Pali canon. It commemorates the life, verse reflections, and passing of the Buddha's foster mother and founder of the bhikkhunī order, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī. An English translation of the text by Jonathan S. Walters was published in Donald S. Lopez's *Buddhism in Practice* (1995) [Piya Tan 2002/2004]. In modern scholarship on Buddhist iconographic traditions, specific verses from this apadāna (such as verse 138 in the Navanālandā Mahāvihāra edition) have been cited regarding auspicious signs and symbols—including the banner, *vardhamāna*, *vajra*, and goad (*aṅkusa*)—found upon the body, hands, or feet of the Buddha [Skilling, Symbols On The Body Feet Hands Of Buddha].
